title: Engine Emission Control — Component Location
introduction:
The positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve regulates crankcase-vapor flow into the intake. Combustion gases that slip past the piston rings are called blow-by; ventilation carries them away instead of letting pressure and contamination build up. Think of the valve as a traffic controller for those vapors.

I use the belt and pulleys at the bottom of this drawing to get my bearings, then locate the cyan-highlighted fitting on the cover at the left of the illustration. Match its callout to the accompanying table. That position describes the picture, not a vehicle-side designation. This reference identifies the valve; it provides no removal sequence or diagnostic test.

edits.why: Match this engine designation before using the illustration. The highlighted valve controls crankcase-vapor flow; its connecting hoses and any oil separator have related but distinct jobs.
